models_evaluated: regulatory-cleared commercially available AI software for cervical spine fracture prioritization on CT

links.outcome: Fractures missed by AI prioritization tool, and their clinical relevance
links.effect: 22 fractures missed by AI, of which 5 required stabilizing therapy; sensitivity 89.8% (95% CI 84.2-94.0%), NPV 99.1%.
links.quote: 22 fractures were missed by AI of which 5 required stabilizing therapy.

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI versus radiology reference standard
links.effect: Sensitivity 89.8%, specificity 95.3%, PPV 63.0%; clinically relevant fractures missed despite high accuracy.
links.quote: Although AI-assisted workflow prioritization of cervical spine fractures on CT shows high diagnostic accuracy, clinically relevant cases were missed.

models_evaluated: Commercially available, regulatory-cleared cervical spine fracture detection AI application (name not reported)

links.outcome: Time between CT acquisition and first opening of the scan
links.effect: DNT was 18 % (5 min) shorter overall and 46 % (16 min) shorter for fracture-positive scans in the prospective cohort.
links.quote: In scans positive for cervical spine fracture according to the reference standard, DNT was 46 % (16 min) shorter in the prospective cohort.
